from PIL import Image
import colorsys

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w, h = im.size
px = im.load()

# Collect stripe colors (average across height since it's uniform per column)
cols = []
for x in range(w):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(h):
        p = px[x,y]
        r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r//h, g//h, b//h))

import statistics
def hsv(c):
    hh,ss,vv = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(c[0]/255, c[1]/255, c[2]/255)
    return hh*360, ss, vv

sats, vals, hues = [], [], []
for c in cols:
    hh,ss,vv = hsv(c)
    sats.append(ss); vals.append(vv); hues.append(hh if ss>0.05 else None)

print("Mean RGB:", tuple(round(statistics.mean(c[i] for c in cols),1) for i in range(3)))
print("Mean sat:", round(statistics.mean(sats),3), " Mean val:", round(statistics.mean(vals),3))
print("Median sat:", round(statistics.median(sats),3), " Median val:", round(statistics.median(vals),3))

# how many stripes are very dark (black-ish), very bright
dark = sum(1 for v in vals if v < 0.15)
bright = sum(1 for v in vals if v > 0.75)
print(f"Very dark stripes: {dark}/{w} ({100*dark/w:.1f}%), bright: {bright}/{w} ({100*bright/w:.1f}%)")

# hue histogram for saturated stripes
from collections import Counter
hue_bins = Counter()
for hhh in hues:
    if hhh is not None:
        hue_bins[int(hhh//30)*30] += 1
print("Hue bins (deg:count):", dict(sorted(hue_bins.items())))

# most common exact colors
cnt = Counter(cols)
print("Top 15 stripe colors:")
for c, n in cnt.most_common(15):
    print(f"  RGB{c} x{n}")

# Desaturated? what fraction has sat < 0.25
low_sat = sum(1 for s in sats if s < 0.25)
print(f"Low-sat (<0.25) stripes: {low_sel if False else low_sat}/{w} = {100*low_sat/w:.1f}%")
EOF

import colorsys

    for y in range(h):
        p = px[x,y]
        r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r//h, g//h, b//h))

# 10 timeline chunks: mean color, brightness, sat
print("Timeline profile (10% chunks): pos | meanRGB | val | sat")
for i in range(10):
    seg = cols[i*w//10:(i+1)*w//10]
    r = sum(c[0] for c in seg)/len(seg); g = sum(c[1] for c in seg)/len(seg); b = sum(c[2] for c in seg)/len(seg)
    hh,ss,vv = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r/255,g/255,b/255)
    print(f"  {i*10}-{(i+1)*10}% | RGB({r:.0f},{g:.0f},{b:.0f}) | v={vv:.2f} s={ss:.2f}")

def clusters(xs, gap=15):
    out=[]
    for x in xs:
        if out and x-out[-1][-1]<=gap: out[-1].append(x)
        else: out.append([x])
    return [(c[0], c[-1], len(c)) for c in out if len(c)>=2]
print("Blue clusters (start,end,count):", clusters(blues))

greens = [x for x,c in enumerate(cols) if (lambda hh,ss,vv: ss>0.15 and 60<=hh<180)(*colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(c[0]/255,c[1]/255,c[2]/255))]
print("Green/teal clusters:", clusters(greens, gap=5))

brightest = sorted(range(w), key=lambda x: -max(cols[x]))[:10]
print("Brightest stripes at x:", sorted(brightest), [cols[x] for x in sorted(brightest)])

# long runs of black (scene cuts / very dark sections)
darks = [x for x,c in enumerate(cols) if max(c) < 25]
print("Near-black cluster spans:", [(a,b,n) for a,b,n in clusters(darks, gap=10) if b-a > 8])

from PIL import Image

w, h = im.size
px = im.load()

    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(h):
        p = px[x,y]
        r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r//h, g//h, b//h))

# first and last 15 stripes
print("\nfirst 15:", cols[:15])
print("last 15:", cols[-15:])

***The Illusionist*** is a 2006 American [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film") [mystery film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_film "Mystery film") written and directed by [Neil Burger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Burger "Neil Burger") and starring [Edward Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Norton "Edward Norton"), [Paul Giamatti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Giamatti "Paul Giamatti"), and [Jessica Biel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Biel "Jessica Biel"). Based loosely on [Steven Millhauser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Millhauser "Steven Millhauser")'s short story "[Eisenheim the Illusionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenheim_the_Illusionist "Eisenheim the Illusionist")", it tells the story of Eisenheim, a [magician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_\(illusion\) "Magic (illusion)") in turn-of-the-century [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), who reunites with his childhood love, a woman far above his social standing. It also depicts a fictionalized version of the [Mayerling incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayerling_incident "Mayerling incident").[\[7\]](#cite_note-FYC-7)

It premiered at the [2006 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Sundance_Film_Festival "2006 Sundance Film Festival") and opened the 2006 [Seattle International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_International_Film_Festival "Seattle International Film Festival"); it was distributed in limited release to theaters on August 18, 2006 and expanded nationwide on September 1\. It was a critical and commercial success.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 1889 [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), [Austria-Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary"), a magician named Eisenheim is arrested by Chief Inspector Walter Uhl of the Vienna Police during a magic show involving [necromancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necromancy "Necromancy"). Later, Uhl explains the story of Eisenheim's life to Crown Prince Leopold.

Eisenheim, born Eduard Abramovich to a carpenter, became interested in magic after a chance encounter with a travelling elderly magician. Whilst learning the basics, he fell in love with Sophie, the [Duchess von Teschen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Teschen "Duchy of Teschen"), but they were forbidden to see each other as Eduard was a peasant. They kept meeting secretly but were eventually caught and separated by force. Eisenheim subsequently departed Austria and spent the next 15 years travelling the world and studying magic before returning to Vienna to perform. During one performance, he encounters the adult Sophie and learns that she is expected to marry the Crown Prince Leopold, who, it is rumored, is brutal towards women and even murdered one. Leopold invites Eisenheim to give a private performance at the palace. During the performance, Eisenheim humiliates the prince in front of the royal guests; in response, he is banned from performing again in Vienna. When Sophie comes to offer him help, they have sex. Eisenheim asks her to flee with him, but she is afraid they will be caught and executed. She reveals that the Crown Prince is planning a *[coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d'état "Coup d'état")* against his elderly father, the [Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Joseph_I "Franz Joseph I").

At the [Mayerling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayerling "Mayerling") hunting lodge, Sophie tries to end her engagement to Leopold. Her body is discovered the next morning in the [Vienna Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_Woods "Vienna Woods"), an unknown man blamed. This throws Eisenheim into depression. He buys a theatre and begins a new series of shows focusing on the summoning of dead spirits. Leopold secretly attends one, during which Eisenheim summons the spirit of Sophie, who says that someone in the theater is her murderer. Leopold, unnerved, orders Uhl to arrest Eisenheim for fraud, but Eisenheim avoids jail by confessing to the public that his show is an illusion.

Eisenheim is threatened that if he summons Sophie in his next performance, he will be imprisoned. Uhl attends the performance, and in spite of the warnings, Eisenheim summons Sophie again. Uhl storms the stage with his officers, but to the shock of the audience, Eisenheim himself is revealed to be a spirit when Uhl's hand passes through him.

Uhl reveals to Leopold that he has found evidence—a jewel from Leopold's sword and Sophie's locket—which could implicate Leopold in Sophie's murder. Uhl further reveals that he knew of Leopold's plan all along, but said nothing as he thought Leopold would be a better emperor and Uhl could secure a promotion to Chief of Police by supporting him. However, Sophie's death made him realize that the Crown Prince is unfit to rule, so he changed his mind and informed the Emperor and the [Austro-Hungarian General Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_General_Staff "Austro-Hungarian General Staff") of Leopold's conspiracy. As officers of the imperial guard of the [Austro-Hungarian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Army "Austro-Hungarian Army") arrive, Leopold shoots himself in the head. Uhl leaves and places Sophie's locket in his pocket.

As a boy approaches Uhl, he is jostled by a bearded man in a long coat. The boy gives him a package containing Eisenheim's notebook about the Orange Tree trick, which Uhl had been unable to figure out. He shouts to the boy asking who gave him the notebook, and the boy replies, "Herr Eisenheim." He realizes the person who jostled him, Eisenheim, stole the locket. He gives chase, but Eisenheim escapes by boarding a train. Uhl realizes the jostling and the notebook are a message from the illusionist, and he begins to rethink recent events. He concludes that Sophie and Eisenheim staged her death so that she could be free of Leopold, with her ghostly apparitions being nothing more than illusions. Uhl laughs delightedly at the brilliance of their plan. Far away, Sophie and Eisenheim start a new life together in a cabin by a beautiful mountain. Eisenheim places Sophie's locket in her palm.

The script was based loosely on "[Eisenheim the Illusionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenheim_the_Illusionist "Eisenheim the Illusionist")", a [short story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_story "Short story") by [Steven Millhauser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Millhauser "Steven Millhauser") from his 1990 collection *[The Barnum Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Barnum_Museum "The Barnum Museum")*. Together with *[The Prestige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prestige "The Prestige")* and *[Scoop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoop_\(2006_film\) "Scoop (2006 film)")*, *The Illusionist* was one of three films in 2006 to explore the world of [stage magicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_\(illusion\) "Magic (illusion)"), and the only one not to feature [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson") and [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") in its cast.

Magic consultancy and technical advice during the production was supplied by [James Freedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Freedman_\(pickpocket\) "James Freedman (pickpocket)"), [Ricky Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Jay "Ricky Jay"), Michael Weber, and [Scott Penrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Penrose "Scott Penrose"). Director [Neil Burger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Burger "Neil Burger") wrote, "Starting in pre-production, James (Freedman) became a major collaborator: brainstorming, designing, and refining everything from small sleight of hand tricks to major narrative set pieces. He worked with [Edward Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Norton "Edward Norton") preparing him for his stage performances and acted as a hand double in various scenes. His contribution was enormous."[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) [Aaron Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Taylor-Johnson "Aaron Taylor-Johnson"), who plays the teenage Eduard in the beginning of the film, also learned how to do the ball trick seen in those scenes.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The original story, on which the movie is based, does not include the artifice of the [protagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protagonist "Protagonist") framing the crown prince for murder.

Although the film is set in [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria"), it was filmed mostly in the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic"). The city of [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna") is represented in the film by [Tábor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tábor "Tábor") and [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), while the scenes set in Eisenheim's childhood village were shot in [Český Krumlov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Český_Krumlov "Český Krumlov"). The Crown Prince's castle is actually the historical fortress of [Konopiště](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konopiště "Konopiště") (near [Benešov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benešov "Benešov")), formerly the home of [Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand_of_Austria "Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria"). The front gates of Leopold's Vienna palace (the [Hofburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hofburg "Hofburg")) were actually the front gates of [Prague Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague_Castle "Prague Castle"). All other shots were at [Barrandov Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrandov_Studios "Barrandov Studios") in Prague.

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

As of June 29, 2008 the film had earned worldwide box office receipts of $87,892,388, including $39,868,642 in the United States, exceeding its reported $16.5 million budget.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) In the first five months after it was released on DVD in January 2007, it earned $35.99 million in rental revenue.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

*The Illusionist* received mostly positive reviews. [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gives it an approval score of 73% based on 194 reviews, with an average rating of 6\.94/10. The consensus reads, "*The Illusionist* is an engrossing, well-crafted story of mystery, magic and intrigue that is certain to enchant, if not hypnotize, audiences."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a score of 68 out of 100 based on 37 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

[Jonathan Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rosenbaum "Jonathan Rosenbaum")'s review in *The Chicago Reader* praised Paul Giamatti's performance of "a character who feels sympathy for the magician but owes allegiance to Leopold and is therefore divided and compromised ... Giamatti's performance is subtle, expressive, and richly nuanced."[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) [Stephen Holden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Holden "Stephen Holden"), in his review for *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, praised Edward Norton's role, which, according to him, "perfectly fits his disturbing inscrutability".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) *Variety* wrote that [Jessica Biel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Biel "Jessica Biel") "is entirely stunning enough to fight to the death over".[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") rated 3\.5/4 and wrote that, "The movie sets up a fascinating parable about art, religion and politics, and the misty boundaries between them".[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

Director of Photography [Dick Pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Pope_\(cinematographer\) "Dick Pope (cinematographer)") earned a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), losing at the [79th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Academy_Awards "79th Academy Awards") to [Guillermo Navarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_Navarro "Guillermo Navarro"), cinematographer for *[Pan's Labyrinth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan's_Labyrinth "Pan's Labyrinth")*.

## Adaptations

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Adaptations")\]

On October 14, 2014, it was announced that [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") was developing a TV series based on the film.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

In June 2020, a Japanese musical adaptation starring [Haruma Miura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haruma_Miura "Haruma Miura"), Naoto Kaiho, and Reika Manaki was announced and set to run from December 2020 to January 2021; however, following Miura's death in July 2020, the project was put on hold.[\[19\]](#cite_note-natalie_2020-06-08-19) In January 2021 it was performed in concert format starring Naoto Kaiho, Reika Manaki and others.

Further information: [ja:イリュージョニスト (ミュージカル)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/イリュージョニスト%20\(ミュージカル\) "ja:イリュージョニスト (ミュージカル)")

On October 28, 2024, it was announced that composer [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber") will be adapting the film into a stage musical with [Chris Terrio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Terrio "Chris Terrio") as book writer and [Bruno Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Major "Bruno Major") as lyricist. [Jamie Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Lloyd_\(director\) "Jamie Lloyd (director)") is also attached to direct the musical with Michael Harrison co-producing with Lloyd Webber (as part of Lloyd Webber Harrison Musicals). Further creatives are to be announced as well as plans to open the production in either [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") or on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre").[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

***The Illusionist*** is a 2006 American [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film") [mystery film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_film "Mystery film") written and directed by [Neil Burger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Burger "Neil Burger") and starring [Edward Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Norton "Edward Norton"), [Paul Giamatti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Giamatti "Paul Giamatti"), and [Jessica Biel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Biel "Jessica Biel"). Based loosely on [Steven Millhauser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Millhauser "Steven Millhauser")'s short story "[Eisenheim the Illusionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenheim_the_Illusionist "Eisenheim the Illusionist")", it tells the story of Eisenheim, a [magician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_\(illusion\) "Magic (illusion)") in turn-of-the-century [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), who reunites with his childhood love, a woman far above his social standing. It also depicts a fictionalized version of the [Mayerling incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayerling_incident "Mayerling incident").[\[7\]](#cite_note-FYC-7)

It premiered at the [2006 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Sundance_Film_Festival "2006 Sundance Film Festival") and opened the 2006 [Seattle International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_International_Film_Festival "Seattle International Film Festival"); it was distributed in limited release to theaters on August 18, 2006 and expanded nationwide on September 1\. It was a critical and commercial success.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 1889 [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), [Austria-Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary"), a magician named Eisenheim is arrested by Chief Inspector Walter Uhl of the Vienna Police during a magic show involving [necromancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necromancy "Necromancy"). Later, Uhl explains the story of Eisenheim's life to Crown Prince Leopold.

Eisenheim, born Eduard Abramovich to a carpenter, became interested in magic after a chance encounter with a travelling elderly magician. Whilst learning the basics, he fell in love with Sophie, the [Duchess von Teschen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Teschen "Duchy of Teschen"), but they were forbidden to see each other as Eduard was a peasant. They kept meeting secretly but were eventually caught and separated by force. Eisenheim subsequently departed Austria and spent the next 15 years travelling the world and studying magic before returning to Vienna to perform. During one performance, he encounters the adult Sophie and learns that she is expected to marry the Crown Prince Leopold, who, it is rumored, is brutal towards women and even murdered one. Leopold invites Eisenheim to give a private performance at the palace. During the performance, Eisenheim humiliates the prince in front of the royal guests; in response, he is banned from performing again in Vienna. When Sophie comes to offer him help, they have sex. Eisenheim asks her to flee with him, but she is afraid they will be caught and executed. She reveals that the Crown Prince is planning a *[coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d'état "Coup d'état")* against his elderly father, the [Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Joseph_I "Franz Joseph I").

At the [Mayerling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayerling "Mayerling") hunting lodge, Sophie tries to end her engagement to Leopold. Her body is discovered the next morning in the [Vienna Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_Woods "Vienna Woods"), an unknown man blamed. This throws Eisenheim into depression. He buys a theatre and begins a new series of shows focusing on the summoning of dead spirits. Leopold secretly attends one, during which Eisenheim summons the spirit of Sophie, who says that someone in the theater is her murderer. Leopold, unnerved, orders Uhl to arrest Eisenheim for fraud, but Eisenheim avoids jail by confessing to the public that his show is an illusion.

Eisenheim is threatened that if he summons Sophie in his next performance, he will be imprisoned. Uhl attends the performance, and in spite of the warnings, Eisenheim summons Sophie again. Uhl storms the stage with his officers, but to the shock of the audience, Eisenheim himself is revealed to be a spirit when Uhl's hand passes through him.

Uhl reveals to Leopold that he has found evidence—a jewel from Leopold's sword and Sophie's locket—which could implicate Leopold in Sophie's murder. Uhl further reveals that he knew of Leopold's plan all along, but said nothing as he thought Leopold would be a better emperor and Uhl could secure a promotion to Chief of Police by supporting him. However, Sophie's death made him realize that the Crown Prince is unfit to rule, so he changed his mind and informed the Emperor and the [Austro-Hungarian General Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_General_Staff "Austro-Hungarian General Staff") of Leopold's conspiracy. As officers of the imperial guard of the [Austro-Hungarian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Army "Austro-Hungarian Army") arrive, Leopold shoots himself in the head. Uhl leaves and places Sophie's locket in his pocket.

As a boy approaches Uhl, he is jostled by a bearded man in a long coat. The boy gives him a package containing Eisenheim's notebook about the Orange Tree trick, which Uhl had been unable to figure out. He shouts to the boy asking who gave him the notebook, and the boy replies, "Herr Eisenheim." He realizes the person who jostled him, Eisenheim, stole the locket. He gives chase, but Eisenheim escapes by boarding a train. Uhl realizes the jostling and the notebook are a message from the illusionist, and he begins to rethink recent events. He concludes that Sophie and Eisenheim staged her death so that she could be free of Leopold, with her ghostly apparitions being nothing more than illusions. Uhl laughs delightedly at the brilliance of their plan. Far away, Sophie and Eisenheim start a new life together in a cabin by a beautiful mountain. Eisenheim places Sophie's locket in her palm.

The script was based loosely on "[Eisenheim the Illusionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenheim_the_Illusionist "Eisenheim the Illusionist")", a [short story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_story "Short story") by [Steven Millhauser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Millhauser "Steven Millhauser") from his 1990 collection *[The Barnum Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Barnum_Museum "The Barnum Museum")*. Together with *[The Prestige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prestige "The Prestige")* and *[Scoop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoop_\(2006_film\) "Scoop (2006 film)")*, *The Illusionist* was one of three films in 2006 to explore the world of [stage magicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_\(illusion\) "Magic (illusion)"), and the only one not to feature [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson") and [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") in its cast.

Magic consultancy and technical advice during the production was supplied by [James Freedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Freedman_\(pickpocket\) "James Freedman (pickpocket)"), [Ricky Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Jay "Ricky Jay"), Michael Weber, and [Scott Penrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Penrose "Scott Penrose"). Director [Neil Burger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Burger "Neil Burger") wrote, "Starting in pre-production, James (Freedman) became a major collaborator: brainstorming, designing, and refining everything from small sleight of hand tricks to major narrative set pieces. He worked with [Edward Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Norton "Edward Norton") preparing him for his stage performances and acted as a hand double in various scenes. His contribution was enormous."[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) [Aaron Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Taylor-Johnson "Aaron Taylor-Johnson"), who plays the teenage Eduard in the beginning of the film, also learned how to do the ball trick seen in those scenes.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The original story, on which the movie is based, does not include the artifice of the [protagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protagonist "Protagonist") framing the crown prince for murder.

Although the film is set in [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria"), it was filmed mostly in the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic"). The city of [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna") is represented in the film by [Tábor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tábor "Tábor") and [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), while the scenes set in Eisenheim's childhood village were shot in [Český Krumlov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Český_Krumlov "Český Krumlov"). The Crown Prince's castle is actually the historical fortress of [Konopiště](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konopiště "Konopiště") (near [Benešov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benešov "Benešov")), formerly the home of [Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand_of_Austria "Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria"). The front gates of Leopold's Vienna palace (the [Hofburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hofburg "Hofburg")) were actually the front gates of [Prague Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague_Castle "Prague Castle"). All other shots were at [Barrandov Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrandov_Studios "Barrandov Studios") in Prague.

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

As of June 29, 2008 the film had earned worldwide box office receipts of $87,892,388, including $39,868,642 in the United States, exceeding its reported $16.5 million budget.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) In the first five months after it was released on DVD in January 2007, it earned $35.99 million in rental revenue.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

*The Illusionist* received mostly positive reviews. [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gives it an approval score of 73% based on 194 reviews, with an average rating of 6\.94/10. The consensus reads, "*The Illusionist* is an engrossing, well-crafted story of mystery, magic and intrigue that is certain to enchant, if not hypnotize, audiences."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a score of 68 out of 100 based on 37 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

[Jonathan Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rosenbaum "Jonathan Rosenbaum")'s review in *The Chicago Reader* praised Paul Giamatti's performance of "a character who feels sympathy for the magician but owes allegiance to Leopold and is therefore divided and compromised ... Giamatti's performance is subtle, expressive, and richly nuanced."[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) [Stephen Holden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Holden "Stephen Holden"), in his review for *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, praised Edward Norton's role, which, according to him, "perfectly fits his disturbing inscrutability".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) *Variety* wrote that [Jessica Biel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Biel "Jessica Biel") "is entirely stunning enough to fight to the death over".[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") rated 3\.5/4 and wrote that, "The movie sets up a fascinating parable about art, religion and politics, and the misty boundaries between them".[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

Director of Photography [Dick Pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Pope_\(cinematographer\) "Dick Pope (cinematographer)") earned a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), losing at the [79th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Academy_Awards "79th Academy Awards") to [Guillermo Navarro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_Navarro "Guillermo Navarro"), cinematographer for *[Pan's Labyrinth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan's_Labyrinth "Pan's Labyrinth")*.

## Adaptations

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Illusionist_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Adaptations")\]

On October 14, 2014, it was announced that [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") was developing a TV series based on the film.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

In June 2020, a Japanese musical adaptation starring [Haruma Miura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haruma_Miura "Haruma Miura"), Naoto Kaiho, and Reika Manaki was announced and set to run from December 2020 to January 2021; however, following Miura's death in July 2020, the project was put on hold.[\[19\]](#cite_note-natalie_2020-06-08-19) In January 2021 it was performed in concert format starring Naoto Kaiho, Reika Manaki and others.

Further information: [ja:イリュージョニスト (ミュージカル)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/イリュージョニスト%20\(ミュージカル\) "ja:イリュージョニスト (ミュージカル)")

On October 28, 2024, it was announced that composer [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber") will be adapting the film into a stage musical with [Chris Terrio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Terrio "Chris Terrio") as book writer and [Bruno Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Major "Bruno Major") as lyricist. [Jamie Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Lloyd_\(director\) "Jamie Lloyd (director)") is also attached to direct the musical with Michael Harrison co-producing with Lloyd Webber (as part of Lloyd Webber Harrison Musicals). Further creatives are to be announced as well as plans to open the production in either [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") or on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre").[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

The Wikipedia plot confirms the fit. My color analysis maps cleanly onto *The Illusionist*'s structure:

**What the barcode shows:**
- A **uniformly dark, warm sepia-brown palette** (mean brightness 0.25, hue ~20°, 18% near-black stripes, only ONE stripe brighter than 0.75 in the entire film) — the signature of the film's celebrated sepia "faded old photograph" grade with heavy vignetting (Dick Pope's Oscar-nominated cinematography)
- **Night-blue runs** at ~41%, ~54–59%, and ~75% — matching the lantern-lit theatre spirit-show sequences and palace night scenes
- A single **muted olive-green woods run at ~42.3–43.5%** — matching the Vienna Woods (Sophie's ride / her body's discovery at roughly the midpoint)
- A **vivid blue scene at ~97% followed by pale gray-blue**, then black credits — matching the train chase and the pale mountain-cabin epilogue ("a cabin by a beautiful mountain")

**Why the other candidates fail:**
- *Knight of Cups*, *On Golden Pond*, *Candy*: full of bright beach/lake/sky footage — this barcode has essentially none
- *Sophie's Choice*: has extended bright green-gold Polish summer flashbacks — absent here
- *Boys from Brazil*: bright Austrian snow and sunlit plantation scenes — absent
- *Prom Night*: disco pinks/reds and bright gym scenes; *Detachment* / *Half Nelson*: bright daylight classrooms — the palette here is far too uniformly dark sepia
- *Beauty and the Beast (2014)*: its famous **red dress** would produce saturated red stripes (there are none), plus bright snow-garden and golden-finale footage

The Illusionist is the only candidate that is entirely dark, warm sepia-brown with no bright sequences at all, blue night shows in the middle, a woods scene near the midpoint, and a pale-blue ending before credits.

Answer: D
